title: Beetroot, Orange and Watercress Salad
subtitle: Earthy beetroot and juicy orange on a bed of peppery watercress
excerpt: Roasted or ready-cooked beetroot with peeled orange segments on a pile of watercress, dressed in a light orange and balsamic vinaigrette. A vivid, peppery salad that works as a starter or a side.
sourceNotes: Beetroot and orange is a combination that appears in British and French salad cookbooks from at least the 1970s, pairing the earthy sweetness of the root with the acidity of citrus. Watercress, one of Britain's oldest cultivated salad plants, provides a peppery base. The combination became a popular British starter salad from the 1990s onward, particularly in the winter months when both beetroot and navel oranges are in season.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Keep the components separate and assemble just before serving; beetroot stains the watercress and orange if left to sit.

content.text: Beetroot, orange and watercress is a salad that looks dramatic for very little effort, especially if you use a mix of red and golden beetroot. Ready-cooked vacuum-packed beetroot (not in vinegar) works perfectly here. The orange should be segmented cleanly so it is all flesh and no membrane or pith. The watercress needs to be fresh and peppery: limp watercress makes a dull base.

items.prepNote: cooked and peeled (about 400 g), cut into wedges
freshly squeezed, from the oranges above

content.text: Whisk together {{balsamic-vinegar}} of balsamic vinegar, {{orange-juice}} of freshly squeezed orange juice, {{olive-oil}} of olive oil, {{dijon-mustard}} of Dijon mustard, {{sea-salt-fine}} of salt and {{black-pepper}} of pepper. Arrange the watercress on a large plate or shallow bowl. Arrange the beetroot wedges and orange segments over the watercress. Drizzle the dressing over. Scatter with walnuts and crumbled goat's cheese if using. Serve immediately.

items.fix: Assemble at the last moment. If using pre-cooked beetroot, pat it dry with kitchen paper before plating.
Cut away the peel and all white pith with a knife before segmenting. Run the knife along the membrane of each segment to release just the flesh.

content.text: Beetroot, orange and watercress is a winter salad in the British tradition, made when both root vegetables and citrus are at their best. It has been a restaurant starter staple since the 1990s, appearing on menus ranging from gastro pubs to smart bistros. The goat's cheese and walnut additions are optional but traditional companions that push it towards a full-meal starter.
